body:
**Redaction gap: `/i` case-folds the negated class, so uppercase-preceded secret pairs evade detection.**

```js
/(^|[^a-z])(key|token|password|secret)=\S+/i
```

In JS, the `i` flag case-folds character-class ranges — including negated ones. `[^a-z]` under `/i` behaves as `[^a-zA-Z]`, so the guard fails to match whenever the character immediately before `key|token|password|secret=` is an *uppercase* letter. Any secret-shaped attribute value written in PascalCase/camelCase — `MyToken=abc123...`, `APIKey=...`, `DBPassword=...`, `AuthSecret=...` — silently passes `attributeViolations` with no violation, even though it is exactly the "key=/token=/password=/secret= pair" shape this table is meant to catch per the PR's own definition.

Verified directly against this policy (not simulated): `attributeViolations({ detail: "my_token=abc123def456" })` returns a violation, but `attributeViolations({ detail: "MyToken=abc123def456" })` returns `[]` — same shape, only the preceding character's case differs.

Since the accompanying test table only exercises lowercase-prefixed and all-lowercase cases (`api_key=`, `GITHUB_TOKEN=` — underscore-preceded, `monkey=` — lowercase-preceded), this gap isn't caught by the current suite.

A fix that avoids the case-fold pitfall, e.g. matching only a preceding boundary explicitly: `/(^|[^A-Za-z])(key|token|password|secret)=\S+/i` (spell out both cases in the class, since `/i` no longer needs to fold what's already listed) — or drop the class from the case-insensitive group entirely and handle case separately.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=Fix%20the%20redaction%20regex%20in%20packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Ftelemetry.policy.ts%20line%2046%20on%20branch%20issue-74-telemetry-record-vocabulary-and-policy%3A%20the%20pattern%20%2F(%5E%7C%5B%5Ea-z%5D)(key%7Ctoken%7Cpassword%7Csecret)%3D%5CS%2B%2Fi%20fails%20to%20redact%20secret-shaped%20values%20preceded%20by%20an%20uppercase%20letter%20(e.g.%20%22MyToken%3Dabc123%22)%20because%20the%20%2Fi%20flag%20case-folds%20the%20negated%20class%20%5B%5Ea-z%5D%20to%20%5B%5Ea-zA-Z%5D.%20Fix%20by%20spelling%20out%20both%20cases%20explicitly%3A%20%2F(%5E%7C%5BA-Za-z%5D)(key%7Ctoken%7Cpassword%7Csecret)%3D%5CS%2B%2Fi%20and%20add%20a%20test%20case%20for%20an%20uppercase-preceded%20pair%20like%20%22MyToken%3Dabc123def456%22.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

body:
**Uncaught crash on `attributes: null` / `labels: null` instead of a rejection**

`record.attributes !== undefined` (here) and `record.labels !== undefined` (line 150) both let `null` through to `Object.entries(...)`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` for a `null` argument. Reproduced directly against this policy:

```ts
recordViolations({ ...valid, attributes: null } as unknown as TelemetryRecord); // throws
recordViolations({ ...valid, signal: "metric", value: 1, labels: null } as unknown as TelemetryRecord); // throws
```

This module's own header states the contract: "Every validity check rejects, never mutates — an invalid record is dropped whole" (telemetry.policy.ts:1-8). A malformed record with `attributes: null`/`labels: null` — plausible once this gate runs on parsed/untrusted JSON in #77 — crashes the caller instead of being classified as a violation, unlike `record.subject?.issue_number`, which is null-safe via optional chaining. Guard with `record.attributes != null` / `record.labels != null` (or treat a non-object as a violation) so malformed input is rejected rather than throwing.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=Fix%20packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Ftelemetry.policy.ts%3A%20recordViolations%20calls%20attributeViolations(record.attributes)%20and%20metricLabelViolations(record.labels)%20whenever%20the%20field%20is%20not%20undefined%2C%20but%20record.attributes%3A%20null%20or%20record.labels%3A%20null%20reach%20Object.entries(null)%20and%20throw%20a%20TypeError%20instead%20of%20being%20rejected%20as%20a%20violation.%20Guard%20both%20checks%20(lines%20~129%20and%20~150)%20so%20null%20is%20treated%20as%20invalid%20input%20and%20pushes%20a%20violation%20instead%20of%20crashing%2C%20consistent%20with%20the%20module%27s%20%22reject%2C%20never%20mutate%22%20contract.&repo=egoisutolabs/score

**P2: `project` is only truthiness-checked, not type-checked**

```ts
if (!record.project) violations.push("missing project");
```

A record with a non-string but truthy `project` (e.g. `project: 123`) produces zero violations — reproduced: `recordViolations({ ...valid, project: 123 } as unknown as TelemetryRecord)` returns `[]`. Every other field that isn't naturally caught by the TS type still gets an explicit runtime check here for exactly this reason (`v: 2 as never`, `signal: "log" as never` are both in the test table), and `project` is one of the PR's own "valid record" fields (`v: 1`, RFC 3339 `ts`, `signal`, score-namespaced `name`, `project`) plus the key used in `TelemetryCursor`/`TelemetryFilter`. A non-string value here would still pass this gate and later corrupt cursor/filter matching. Lower severity than the null-crash above since it degrades rather than throws, but worth a `typeof record.project !== "string"` check alongside the existing truthiness check.

body:
**Non-`null` non-object `attributes` still passes the gate with zero violations**

The `attributes === null` guard only catches `null`. Any other non-object shape from untrusted/malformed JSON — a string, number, boolean, or array — reaches `attributeViolations(attributes)` via `Object.entries(...)`, which doesn't throw for these but also doesn't detect anything wrong:

```ts
recordViolations({ ...valid, attributes: "foo" });   // []  (Object.entries("foo") walks chars)
recordViolations({ ...valid, attributes: 42 });       // []  (Object.entries(42) === [])
recordViolations({ ...valid, attributes: true });     // []  (Object.entries(true) === [])
recordViolations({ ...valid, attributes: ["a","b"] }); // []  (treated as {0:"a",1:"b"})
```

Verified directly against this policy (not simulated) — all four return `[]`, i.e. the record is accepted as valid despite `attributes` never being the declared `Readonly<Record<string, ...>>` shape. This is the same class of bug this exact block was written to fix for `null` (comment at telemetry.policy.ts:149-150: "a null field is malformed input to reject, never a crash") — but the fix only special-cased `null` rather than rejecting any non-plain-object value. Same gap applies to `labels` at telemetry.policy.ts:188-190 (a `labels: 42`/`true`/`[]` metric also returns `[]` — verified).

Since `recordViolations` is the append gate and this module's stated contract is "an invalid record is dropped whole," a malformed `attributes`/`labels` field of the wrong type is currently accepted rather than rejected.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Ftelemetry.policy.ts%20on%20branch%20issue-74-telemetry-record-vocabulary-and-policy%2C%20the%20checks%20at%20lines%20151-153%20(attributes)%20and%20188-190%20(labels)%20only%20special-case%20%60null%60%3A%20%60if%20(attributes%20%3D%3D%3D%20null)%20violations.push(...)%60.%20Any%20other%20non-object%20value%20(string%2C%20number%2C%20boolean%2C%20array)%20reaches%20Object.entries()%20without%20being%20flagged%2C%20so%20e.g.%20%60recordViolations(%7B%20...valid%2C%20attributes%3A%20%22foo%22%20%7D)%60%20returns%20%5B%5D%20instead%20of%20rejecting.%20Replace%20the%20null-only%20check%20with%20a%20proper%20object-shape%20check%2C%20e.g.%20%60typeof%20attributes%20!%3D%3D%20%22object%22%20%7C%7C%20attributes%20%3D%3D%3D%20null%20%7C%7C%20Array.isArray(attributes)%60%2C%20applied%20to%20both%20the%20attributes%20and%20labels%20branches%2C%20and%20add%20test%20cases%20for%20string%2Fnumber%2Fboolean%2Farray%20values.&repo=egoisutolabs/score

body:
**P2: `status` is declared as an enum but never runtime-validated, unlike every sibling span field**

`TelemetrySpan.status?: "ok" | "error"` (telemetry.interface.ts:59) is never referenced anywhere in `telemetry.policy.ts` (confirmed via `grep -rn status packages/core/src/telemetry` — the only hit is the interface declaration). This span block validates `span_id`, `parent_span_id`, and `duration_ms` at runtime specifically because "untrusted JSON can carry null or a number where the type says string" (comment at line 172) — the same rationale applies to `status`: a parsed/untrusted record with `status: "pending"` or `status: 123` satisfies the TS type at compile time only and passes `recordViolations` with zero violations, so an out-of-vocabulary status value is accepted and stored, corrupting downstream status-based aggregation exactly the way the now-fixed `duration_ms`/`span_id`/`parent_span_id`/subject-number gaps did.

Unlike `TelemetrySubject`'s `session`/`branch` strings — which are deliberately left unchecked with an explicit comment ("Subject strings pass through untouched (identity is dispatch's)") — there's no such rationale documented for skipping `status`, so this reads as an oversight rather than a design choice.

Suggest adding to the span block: `if (record.status !== undefined && record.status !== "ok" && record.status !== "error") violations.push("status must be \"ok\" or \"error\"");`

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Ftelemetry.policy.ts%2C%20the%20span%20validation%20block%20(around%20line%20171-187)%20checks%20span_id%2C%20parent_span_id%2C%20and%20duration_ms%20at%20runtime%20because%20untrusted%2Fparsed%20JSON%20can%20violate%20the%20TS%20type%2C%20but%20never%20checks%20%60record.status%60%20even%20though%20%60TelemetrySpan.status%60%20is%20declared%20as%20%60%22ok%22%20%7C%20%22error%22%60%20in%20telemetry.interface.ts%3A59.%20Add%20a%20check%3A%20%60if%20(record.status%20!%3D%3D%20undefined%20%26%26%20record.status%20!%3D%3D%20%22ok%22%20%26%26%20record.status%20!%3D%3D%20%22error%22)%20violations.push(%22status%20must%20be%20%5C%22ok%5C%22%20or%20%5C%22error%5C%22%22)%3B%60%20and%20add%20a%20test%20case%20for%20an%20out-of-vocabulary%20status%20value%20like%20%22pending%22%20or%20a%20numeric%20status.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

body:
**P2: a non-object `subject` passes the gate with zero violations — the same gap already fixed for `attributes`/`labels`/`body`, missed for `subject` itself.**

`record.subject?.issue_number` and `record.subject?.pull_request_number` (lines 175–181) are the only runtime checks on `subject`. Both use optional chaining, which only short-circuits on `null`/`undefined` — for any other non-object shape (`string`, `number`, `array`, `boolean`), `.issue_number` simply reads `undefined` off the value with no error, so the field is silently skipped and the record is accepted as valid.

Reproduced directly against this policy (verified, not simulated) — all return `[]`:
```ts
recordViolations({ ...valid, subject: "junk" });   // []
recordViolations({ ...valid, subject: 42 });        // []
recordViolations({ ...valid, subject: ["a"] });      // []
recordViolations({ ...valid, subject: null });       // []
recordViolations({ ...valid, subject: true });       // []
```

This is the identical bug class this PR already fixed multiple times this round for `attributes` (line 170: `if (!isPlainObject(attributes)) violations.push(...)`) and `labels` (line 211), both explicitly justified by the comment at lines 165–167: *"The gate also runs on parsed, untrusted JSON in #77 — any non-object shape here is malformed input to reject, never a crash or a silent pass."* That same rationale applies verbatim to `subject`, but no `isPlainObject(record.subject)` guard exists before the optional-chained field reads, so a malformed `subject` of the wrong type is accepted and stored rather than rejected — inconsistent with the module's stated "an invalid record is dropped whole" contract, and the exact class of gap #77's JSON-parsing path will hit.

Suggest adding a guard before the numeric checks, mirroring the `attributes`/`labels` pattern: `if (record.subject !== undefined && !isPlainObject(record.subject)) violations.push("subject must be an object");`

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Ftelemetry.policy.ts%20on%20branch%20issue-74-telemetry-record-vocabulary-and-policy%2C%20recordViolations%20(around%20lines%20173-181)%20only%20checks%20record.subject%3F.issue_number%20and%20record.subject%3F.pull_request_number%20via%20optional%20chaining%2C%20which%20silently%20skips%20validation%20when%20record.subject%20itself%20is%20a%20non-object%20(string%2C%20number%2C%20array%2C%20boolean)%20rather%20than%20null%2Fundefined%20--%20e.g.%20recordViolations(%7B%20...valid%2C%20subject%3A%20%22junk%22%20%7D)%20returns%20%5B%5D.%20This%20mirrors%20the%20isPlainObject%20guard%20already%20added%20for%20attributes%20(line%20170)%20and%20labels%20(line%20211)%20with%20the%20same%20%22malformed%20input%20from%20%2377%27s%20untrusted%20JSON%20must%20reject%2C%20never%20silently%20pass%22%20rationale.%20Add%20a%20guard%3A%20if%20(record.subject%20!%3D%3D%20undefined%20%26%26%20!isPlainObject(record.subject))%20violations.push(%22subject%20must%20be%20an%20object%22)%3B%20and%20add%20test%20cases%20for%20subject%3A%20%22junk%22%2F42%2F%5B%5D%2Ftrue.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

author: claude[bot]
body:
**Reader permanently stalls at a segment boundary once caught up — new segments are never picked up.**

Repro: a reader calls `read()` and catches all the way up to the exact end of the current (only) segment — `cursor = { segment: "2026-08-15", byte_offset: <file length> }`. Later, the writer rotates to a new day and appends to `2026-08-16.jsonl`. The reader calls `read(cursor)` again with the same stale cursor.

In this call `offset === buffer.length`, so `start === buffer.length` and `pending = buffer.subarray(start)` is empty. `pending.lastIndexOf(NEWLINE)` on an empty buffer returns `-1`, which hits the same branch used for a genuine torn/incomplete tail (line 125-129: `offset = start; break;`). The loop exits immediately without ever reaching the `segments.find((candidate) => candidate > segment)` lookup at line 136, so the reader never advances into `2026-08-16.jsonl` — it returns `{ outcome: "OK", records: [], cursor: <unchanged> }` forever. Because the outcome is `OK` with no warning, a polling reader can't distinguish this from "caught up, no new data" — it silently loses every subsequent day's records.

This contradicts the method's own contract ("Every complete line from the cursor forward, advancing across segments") and the PR's stated purpose ("any reader tails without coordination"). The existing "UTC rotation" test (lines 90-110) doesn't catch this because it only calls `read()` once, after *both* segments already exist — it never exercises a `read()` call that resumes from an already-fully-consumed EOF cursor after a *later* rotation.

Verified with a standalone repro against this branch's code:
```ts
const log = new TelemetryLogService(dir, { project }, time.now); // clock at 2026-08-15T23:59:59Z
log.append(event({ name: "score.run.late" }));
const caughtUp = log.read(log.startCursor()); // fully consumes 2026-08-15.jsonl

time.set("2026-08-16T00:00:00Z");
log.append(event({ name: "score.run.early" })); // rotates to 2026-08-16.jsonl

log.read(caughtUp.cursor);
// => { outcome: "OK", records: [], cursor: <unchanged> }  — "score.run.early" is never seen
```

The root cause is that an empty `pending` (nothing left in the current segment) and a genuinely incomplete tail (some bytes present but no terminating `\n`) both produce `lastNewline === -1` and are treated identically, even though only the latter should stop the scan.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In+packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Ftelemetry-log.service.ts+on+branch+issue-77-append-only-telemetry-log-service%2C+the+read%28%29+method%27s+segment-crossing+loop+%28around+lines+111-140%29+incorrectly+treats+an+empty+%60pending%60+buffer+%28cursor+already+at+exact+EOF+of+a+fully-consumed+segment%29+the+same+as+a+genuine+incomplete+tail%3A+both+produce+%60pending.lastIndexOf%28NEWLINE%29+%3D%3D%3D+-1%60+and+break+out+of+the+loop+without+checking+for+a+newer+segment.+This+means+a+reader+that+catches+up+to+the+exact+end+of+a+segment+before+the+next+day%27s+segment+is+created+will+permanently+stall+and+never+see+later+segments+on+subsequent+read%28%29+calls%2C+silently+returning+OK+with+empty+records+forever.+Fix+the+loop+so+it+distinguishes+%22nothing+left+past+offset+in+this+segment%22+%28should+proceed+to+check+segments.find%28candidate+%3D%3E+candidate+%3E+segment%29%29+from+%22some+unterminated+bytes+past+offset%22+%28genuine+incomplete+tail%2C+should+stop%29.+Add+a+regression+test+that+resumes+from+an+already-fully-consumed+EOF+cursor+after+a+later+rotation+creates+a+new+segment+%28the+existing+%22UTC+rotation%22+test+only+calls+read%28%29+once+after+both+segments+already+exist%2C+so+it+doesn%27t+catch+this%29.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

**Confirmed defect: `#readStageSnapshot`'s catch-all still lets evidence-capture failures reach `merge --abort`, reopening the exact "swallowed capture failure" bug this PR's round-2 fix claims to have closed.**

`#readStageSnapshot` wraps `await this.#stageSnapshotPath()` in the same `try` as `readFile`/`JSON.parse` (git.service.ts:412), so a transient failure of the `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` subprocess call (resource contention, a momentary git lock — realistic right after a supervisor restart, which is precisely when `selfHealStagedMerge` makes the *first* call to this path in a fresh process, before `#gitDir` is cached) is silently treated as "no snapshot" instead of propagating.

Concretely, in `abortMerge` (line 194): if that first `#readStageSnapshot()` call hits this transient failure, `snapshot` comes back `undefined`, so the `if (snapshot !== undefined)` capture block is skipped *without throwing* — `merge --abort` (line 202) then runs anyway. Once the merge is confirmed gone, `sweepStageResidue()` runs; by then `#gitDir` resolves fine (this is a *second*, now-successful call), so it reads the real on-disk snapshot (`{before}`-only, since `stagedIgnored` was never captured), finds `stagedIgnored === undefined`, sweeps nothing, and unconditionally retires the snapshot file (line 246). The residue is left on disk with the evidence gone forever — no MERGE_HEAD, no snapshot — so no future tick or self-heal can ever identify or remove it. This reproduces the exact #92/#68 wedge the PR exists to fix.

The same swallow defeats `stageMerge`'s "finish a pending sweep before overwriting" fix (line 169): a transient failure there makes `pending` read as `undefined`, skipping the pending-sweep check, and the unconditional `#writeStageSnapshot` on the next line overwrites (loses) any real pending residue evidence.

I reproduced this with a script-driven `GitService` (real fixture files + a `CommandRunner` that fails `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` only on its first call, succeeds after): after `abortMerge()`, the gate's `.next/chunk.js` residue remained on disk *and* the snapshot file was deleted — evidence-lost, unrecoverable, matching the trace above. (Verification test not included in the diff — added and run locally, then reverted, per this review's scope.)

Fix direction: `#readStageSnapshot` needs to distinguish "path resolved, file absent/corrupt" (safe to treat as no evidence) from "could not even resolve the snapshot path" (must propagate, per the same principle the round-2 fix established for the write side).

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20packages%2Fcore%2Fsrc%2Fadapters%2Fgit.service.ts%20on%20branch%20issue-92-build-artifacts-landed-in-the-primary-ch%2C%20%23readStageSnapshot%20(around%20line%20409)%20wraps%20%60await%20this.%23stageSnapshotPath()%60%20in%20the%20same%20try%2Fcatch%20as%20readFile%2FJSON.parse%2C%20so%20a%20transient%20failure%20of%20the%20%60git%20rev-parse%20--absolute-git-dir%60%20subprocess%20call%20(which%20only%20happens%20on%20the%20first%20call%20in%20a%20fresh%20process%2C%20before%20%23gitDir%20is%20cached)%20is%20silently%20treated%20as%20%22no%20snapshot%22%20instead%20of%20propagating.%20This%20lets%20abortMerge%20run%20%60merge%20--abort%60%20without%20capturing%20stagedIgnored%2C%20and%20lets%20stageMerge%20overwrite%20a%20pending%20sweep%27s%20evidence%2C%20both%20permanently%20losing%20residue%20evidence%20(reproducing%20the%20%2392%2F%2368%20wedge).%20Fix%20%23readStageSnapshot%20to%20resolve%20the%20snapshot%20path%20(%23stageSnapshotPath())%20OUTSIDE%20the%20try%2Fcatch%20that%20guards%20the%20read%2Fparse%2C%20so%20a%20path-resolution%20failure%20propagates%20instead%20of%20being%20conflated%20with%20%22file%20missing%2Fcorrupt%22.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

body:
**Stale-lock reclaim via `rename` still lets a second contender steal a live lock — the round-5 fix (f514c53) narrows but doesn't close the race the earlier review flagged.**

`rename(oldpath, newpath)` is atomic against *concurrent renames of the same directory entry*, but it has no compare-and-swap semantics against content: it moves whatever currently occupies `lockPath` at the moment it runs, without checking it's still the file that was diagnosed as stale a few lines above (`holder`/`process.kill` check at lines 126–135).

Concrete interleaving (two OS processes, e.g. two `score up`/`restart` calls racing right after a crashed holder):
1. Dead pid `X` owns `lockPath`. Process **A** and process **B** both hit `EEXIST`, both read `holder = X`, both find it dead.
2. **A** runs `rename(lockPath, lockPath.stale)` (moves X's file away), `rm`s the `.stale` file, loops back to the top, and `writeFile(lockPath, pid_A, {flag:"wx"})` succeeds — A now holds a *live* lock and proceeds into `action()`.
3. **B**'s `rename(lockPath, lockPath.stale)` call — still working off its earlier diagnosis of `X` — executes *after* step 2. Since `lockPath` currently exists (it's now A's fresh lock, not X's), the rename succeeds anyway: it blindly moves A's live lock aside. B then `rm`s it, loops back, and `writeFile` succeeds since the path is free again.
4. Both A and B are now past the acquisition loop and running `action()` concurrently on the same project key — exactly the interleaved-mutation state this lock exists to prevent (per the function's own doc comment above).

This requires B's diagnosis-to-rename window to straddle A's full reclaim-and-recreate cycle, which is plausible across two independently-scheduled processes doing real (non-instant) disk I/O, especially in the exact operational scenario this lock is hardened for (a crashed holder plus prompt automated retries). The commit message's claim ("rename succeeds for exactly one contender, so the loser can no longer delete the winner's freshly created lock") only holds when both contenders' renames target the *same, still-present* stale file; it doesn't hold once the winner has already replaced it.

A fix needs to verify the reclaimed file is still the one diagnosed (e.g. re-read/compare content after the rename before trusting it, or use a token/generation check) rather than reclaiming by bare path.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20apps%2Fdaemon%2Fsrc%2Fsupervisor%2Fsupervisor.run.ts%2C%20withProjectLock%27s%20stale-lock%20reclaim%20(around%20line%20139-152%20on%20branch%20issue-93-score-up-key-after-score-down-reports-al)%20uses%20rename(lockPath%2C%20%60%24%7BlockPath%7D.stale%60)%20then%20rm%20to%20reclaim%20a%20dead-holder%20lock.%20This%20doesn%27t%20prevent%20a%20second%20contender%20from%20renaming%20away%20a%20FIRST%20contender%27s%20freshly-created%20live%20lock%2C%20since%20rename%20operates%20on%20the%20path%20not%20the%20diagnosed%20file%27s%20identity%2Fcontent.%20Fix%20by%20verifying%20the%20renamed-aside%20file%27s%20content%20still%20matches%20the%20diagnosed-dead%20pid%20before%20trusting%20the%20reclaim%2C%20or%20use%20some%20other%20compare-and-swap%20mechanism%2C%20and%20add%20a%20regression%20test%20simulating%20two%20interleaved%20reclaimers.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

body:
**The guaranteed `SEGMENT_UNREADABLE` warning is silently dropped when the outbound queue is already at its cap — the client is disconnected with no explanation at all.**

Repro (confirmed with a scratch test against this exact HEAD, `eaffabf`): subscribe with `follow=true`, reach `caught_up`, call `gen.next()` once to enter `follow()` (no backlog yet, so the initial scan finds nothing and the request parks on the idle wait), then append `FOLLOW_QUEUE_LIMIT + 1` (1025) records and let the tailer poll fire. `wakeLoop()` resumes the generator exactly once, dequeuing 1 frame to satisfy the pending `next()`, leaving `queue.length === FOLLOW_QUEUE_LIMIT` (1024) untouched (the consumer never pulls again). Now delete the segment the cursor still names and let the poll fire again: `captureMarks` no longer lists the file, `planReplay` returns `!plan.ok`, and this line calls `enqueue(frameFor(WARNING_EVENT, ..., [{reason: "SEGMENT_UNREADABLE"}]))` — but `queue.length >= FOLLOW_QUEUE_LIMIT` is already true, so `enqueue` (lines 73–83) rejects it, sets `overflowed = true`, and returns `false`. The return value here is never checked. `closing = true` is set anyway (line 99), so the stream still ends cleanly — but the warning that was supposed to be its guaranteed last frame was never queued. In my repro, the drain loop delivered exactly 1023 valid records then hit `done: true` — `warningSeen` stayed `null`.

The same gap exists in the in-scan branch below (lines 111–125): `delivered = enqueue(...)` is computed for the `SEGMENT_UNREADABLE` case too, but the `closing = true` at line 121–124 doesn't check `delivered` before declaring "this warning is the stream's last frame."

Why this matters: the PR's own contract is "one `score.stream.warning` (`SEGMENT_UNREADABLE`) and a clean close," and the comment at lines 95–97 says the client "resumes from an explicit time bound, not from this cursor" specifically *because* it was told the position is unrecoverable. When the warning is dropped, the client instead sees an ordinary disconnect indistinguishable from a plain queue overflow, and per the overflow contract a client would reasonably retry from its last-delivered cursor — which is exactly the cursor this code just decided is unrecoverable. The existing tests never catch this because they each exercise overflow and segment-unreadable in isolation, never with the queue already saturated when the segment disappears.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=Fix%20apps%2Fweb%2Fsrc%2Ftelemetry%2Fstream%2Ffollow.service.ts%20on%20branch%20issue-82-stream-follow-shared-tailers-heartbeat-b%3A%20when%20a%20SEGMENT_UNREADABLE%20warning%20is%20produced%20(the%20!plan.ok%20branch%20around%20line%2094-101%2C%20or%20the%20in-scan%20branch%20around%20line%20111-125)%20while%20the%20outbound%20queue%20is%20already%20at%20FOLLOW_QUEUE_LIMIT%2C%20enqueue()%20silently%20rejects%20the%20warning%20frame%20and%20it%20is%20never%20delivered%20to%20the%20client%2C%20even%20though%20closing%20is%20still%20set%20and%20the%20stream%20ends%20cleanly.%20The%20client%20never%20learns%20the%20cursor%20is%20unrecoverable%20and%20may%20wrongly%20retry%20from%20it.%20Fix%20by%20guaranteeing%20this%20terminal%20warning%20is%20always%20delivered%20(e.g.%20reserve%20room%20for%20it%2C%20or%20let%20it%20bypass%20the%20cap%20since%20it%20is%20provably%20the%20stream%27s%20last%20frame)%20instead%20of%20relying%20on%20the%20ordinary%20enqueue%20path.&repo=egoisutolabs/score)

+# Persisted Trace Contract (v2)
+
+**Status:** normative. This document is the contract between limen and any
+host that persists, reads, or verifies calculation traces — the vendor
+bridge, a compliance tool consuming `Explain` output, or an implementer of a
+custom `limen.AuditSink` / `limen.TraceReader`. A bridge implementer should
+be able to build against traces from this document alone, without reading
+limen internals.
+
+**v2 is the first supported persisted trace contract**
+([trace-schema-v2 D2](../architecture/decisions/trace-schema-v2.md#d2--clean-break-v2-is-the-first-supported-persisted-trace-contract)).
+There is no v1 read path and no up-conversion: a record without
+`schema_version: 2` is refused with a typed error (§5). Pre-v2 records are
+development debris carrying known-incomplete identities — never audit
+history.
+
+Two version fields appear throughout; they are distinct:
+
+| Field | Meaning | Changes when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `schema_version` | envelope **shape** generation (currently `2`) | limen changes the persisted document shape (a compat event) |
+| `version` | **supersede counter** for one `trace_id` (starts at `1`) | a different payload is written under an existing `trace_id` (§4) |
+
+## 1. Guarantees and obligations at a glance
+
+What limen guarantees:
+
+- **Identity completeness.** Two calculations share a `trace_id` only when
+  every result-changing input is identical (§3). Cash-vs-margin,
+  initial-vs-maintenance, or bookkeeping-differing calculations over the
+  same positions get distinct IDs.
+- **Determinism and re-derivability.** The engine is deterministic and
+  clock-free: identical inputs produce identical numbers, so any trace is
+  re-derivable by re-running the calculation. This is also the remedy for an
+  unsupported-version record.
+- **Self-substantiation.** A persisted envelope carries every field its own
+  `trace_id` was derived from, so the ID can be recomputed and verified from
+  the stored record alone — no re-run required (§6). The ID is a seal, not
+  an assertion: a content hash proves, a UUID would only claim.
+- **Pre-computability.** The ID is derivable from the request alone; a host
+  can compute it before calculating.
+- **Supersede, never destroy.** A corrected number never erases the receipt
+  for the old one; `Explain` serves the latest and discloses priors (§4).
+- **Typed errors.** Every read-side failure mode is a sentinel or typed
+  error matched with `errors.Is`/`errors.As` (§5). Messages are not
+  contract.
+
+What the host owns:
+
+- **Storage and durability.** Audit emission is best-effort by contract: a
+  sink error degrades `CalculationResult.AuditStatus`, never fails the
+  calculation. Durability is the sink's job, and the sink is host-supplied
+  (the reference Mongo adapter or a custom one, §7).
+- **Retention.** Trace TTL/archival is host policy
+  ([sdk-result-integrity D5](../architecture/decisions/sdk-result-integrity.md#d5--ttldays-is-deleted-from-runtime-options-retention-is-host-policy-enacted-only-through-migration)),
+  enacted through the host's own migration tooling — for the Mongo adapter,
+  `cmd/migrate` per [operations.md](../operations.md#required-indexes-host-contract).
+- **Version honoring in custom stores.** A custom sink/reader must uphold
+  the versioning and never-destroy obligations of §7 — they are properties
+  of the store, not of limen's code.
+- **Churn monitoring.** Superseding writes are legitimate only around a
+  software upgrade; the host watches the churn signal (§4).
+
+## 2. The envelope
+
+Every emission is one envelope (Go: `limen.AuditEnvelope` on the write side,
+`limen.TraceRecord` on the read side — same fields, same JSON names). Two
+envelope kinds exist, distinguished by role, not shape:
+
+- **Account envelope** — one per calculation. `position_id` carries the
+  account ID (deliberately, so one field keys both envelope kinds);
+  `positions_sha` seals the full position set.
+- **Decomposition envelope** — one per position on the `Decompose: true`
+  path, in addition to the account envelope. `position_id` is the position
+  ID; `positions_sha` is that single position's content seal.
+
+Fields hosts may rely on, by JSON name:
+
+| Field | Type | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `schema_version` | int | always `2`; route/refuse on it before parsing anything else |
+| `version` | int | supersede counter, ≥ 1 (§4) |
+| `trace_id` | string | 32 hex chars, content-derived (§3) |
+| `account_id` | string | owning account |
+| `position_id` | string | account ID on account envelopes; position ID on decomposition envelopes |
+| `account_type` | string | `margin` \| `cash` — participates in the ID |
+| `phase` | string | `initial` \| `maintenance` — participates in the ID |
+| `currency` | string | account currency — participates in the ID |
+| `regime` | object | methodology tag, exactly `{"family": "reg_t_strategy"}` today ([D3](../architecture/decisions/trace-schema-v2.md#d3--regime-identity-is-an-object-with-exactly-one-field-regime-family)); an object so future router-era keys are additive, never a type break. Not part of the ID — the rulebook seal already pins methodology |
+| `positions_sha` | string | SHA-256 (RFC 8785 canonical JSON) of the position content the evaluation saw |
+| `bookkeeping_sha` | string | seal of the bookkeeping scalars; always present — a zero-value bookkeeping seals as its own hash |
+| `policy_sha` | string | seal of host policy facts; **empty exactly when policy was absent from the ID recipe** (§3) |
+| `overlay_rulebook_hash` | string | house overlay rulebook seal; empty on baseline-only calculations |
+| `refdata_sha` | string | reference-data seal; empty on baseline-only calculations (refdata is never read there) |
+| `overrides_sha` | string | seal of the applied override set |
+| `as_of`, `txn_cutoff` | timestamp | bitemporal coordinates, stored truncated to millisecond precision (§3) |
+| `decompose` | bool | which aggregation pipeline ran |
+| `applied_overrides` | array | the exact sorted set `overrides_sha` seals, echoed for auditability |
+| `complete` | bool | true exactly when every position contributed to totals; gate on it before trusting any total in the trace body |
+| `exclusions`, `errors` | arrays | the non-errored gaps and the hard-errored positions, mirroring the calculation result's split |
+| `outcome` | string | derived classification: `matched` \| `not_permitted` \| `incomplete` \| `error` at account level; the trace body's own outcome (e.g. `decomposed`) on decomposition envelopes |
+| `trace` | object | the provenance body: `engine_version`, `rulebook_sha` (participates in the ID), `evaluated_at`, the matched rule / formula / slot-binding detail. Consumed opaquely by this contract except where §3 names a field |
+
+Absent optional fields and empty strings are equivalent (`omitempty`
+encoding); a verifier must treat a missing `refdata_sha` as `""`.
+
+All seals are SHA-256 hex over RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the mapped
+calculation inputs. A host can precompute them for its own snapshot with
+`CalculationSnapshot.Hashes()` and match them against the envelope —
+`positions_sha` and `bookkeeping_sha` are byte-identical to
+`SnapshotHashes.Positions` / `.Bookkeeping` over the same values.
+
+## 3. Identity: what makes two calculations "the same"
+
+([trace-schema-v2 D1](../architecture/decisions/trace-schema-v2.md#d1--trace-identity-is-completed-content-addressing-the-sink-supersedes-with-lineage-never-silently-replaces))
+
+The doctrine: **every result-changing input is folded into the ID; nothing
+else is.** Same ID ⇒ same calculation (same question, same inputs); a
+retried emit of the same evaluation reuses the ID (idempotency is the
+feature). Distinct calculations can never legitimately share an ID.
+
+### 3.1 Account trace ID
+
+The ID is the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256 over an ordered part list,
+each part followed by a NUL byte (`0x00`) so concatenation is unambiguous
+(`("ab","c")` ≠ `("a","bc")`). The parts, in order, from envelope fields:
+
+1. `account_id`
+2. `positions_sha`
+3. `trace.rulebook_sha`
+4. `overlay_rulebook_hash` (empty string on baseline-only)
+5. `refdata_sha` (empty string on baseline-only)
+6. `overrides_sha` (empty string when none applied)
+7. `as_of` — UTC, truncated to millisecond, RFC 3339 with nanosecond
+   formatting (e.g. `2026-09-01T12:00:00Z`; trailing zeros trimmed)
+8. `txn_cutoff` — same formatting
+9. `decompose=<true|false>`
+10. `policy=<policy_sha>` — **present only when `policy_sha` is non-empty**;
+    a policy-free calculation contributes no part at all
+11. `account_type=<account_type>`
+12. `phase=<phase>`
+13. `currency=<currency>`
+14. `bookkeeping=<bookkeeping_sha>` (always present — zero-value
+    bookkeeping seals as its own hash, so absent-vs-zeroed can never
+    collide)
+
+Timestamps are truncated to milliseconds *before* hashing because BSON
+datetimes carry only milliseconds: an envelope read back from the store must
+recompute the same ID from its truncated coordinates as the emitter computed
+from the request.
+
+Deliberately **not** in the ID:
+
+- **The wall clock.** An identical request re-run later produces the same
+  account trace ID — the seal addresses content, not the moment of
+  evaluation, which is what collapses retries.
+- **`engine_version`.** A software upgrade that changes the number for
+  identical inputs keeps the same ID; the new receipt lands as the next
+  supersede version (§4), not a new identity.
+- **`regime.family`.** Today it is derivable from the rulebook seal; it
+  participates in the payload (and therefore in supersede comparison) but
+  not in the ID.
+
+### 3.2 Decomposition trace ID
+
+Per-position envelopes on the decompose path use their own recipe — same
+NUL-separated SHA-256 construction, first 32 hex chars — over:
+
+1. `position_id`
+2. `trace.rulebook_sha`
+3. `account_type`
+4. `phase`
+5. `trace.evaluated_at` — UTC, millisecond-truncated, same formatting as
+   above
+6. `account=<account_id>`
+7. `position_sha=<positions_sha>`
+
+Account identity and the content seal participate because position IDs are
+only unique per account and can be reused for different content. Unlike the
+account ID, this recipe **does** fold the evaluation wall clock
+(`trace.evaluated_at`): re-running a decomposition mints new per-position
+trace IDs. Only the account trace ID is retry-collapsing.
+
+## 4. Supersede semantics: versions and `PriorVersions`
+
+A write whose `trace_id` already exists in the store is handled by payload
+comparison, never by overwrite:
+
+- **Identical payload** (all fields except `version`) → idempotent no-op.
+  Retried emits of the same evaluation cost nothing and leave one record.
+- **Different payload** → the new envelope is stored as the **next
+  `version`** of that `trace_id`. Both receipts are preserved forever;
+  nothing is ever replaced or deleted. Post-§3, a differing payload under
+  the same ID is legitimately possible only when a software upgrade changed
+  the number for identical inputs.

+means "this is the only version". `PriorVersions` is computed at read time,
+never persisted. Any prior is reachable explicitly with
+`ExplainVersion(ctx, traceID, n)` (versions start at 1); a version the store
+does not hold is a not-found error, never the latest served silently.
+
+`PriorVersions > 0` tells a consumer: *the number for this exact calculation
+changed across a software upgrade; earlier receipts exist and are
+retrievable.* A compliance answer built on `Explain` output should disclose
+it rather than present the latest as the only number ever produced.
+
+**Churn is a signal.** A superseding write without a deploy in between means
+the engine produced different numbers for identical inputs — a
+nondeterminism bug. The reference Mongo sink logs a structured warning per
+supersede and exposes an acknowledged-supersede counter
+(`limenmongo.Stores.SupersededTraces()`; see
+[operations.md](../operations.md#audit_traces-ensuretraceindexes)). A custom
+sink must make superseding writes similarly observable.

+## 5. Read surface and typed errors
+
+`Explain` / `ExplainVersion` resolve persisted records through the
+configured `TraceReader`. Match errors with `errors.Is`/`errors.As`;
+messages are not contract.
+
+| Error | Meaning | Consumer action |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `limen.ErrNoTraceReader` | `Explain` called on a Client with no `TraceReader` configured | wiring defect; fix construction |
+| `limen.ErrTraceNotFound` | no record for that `trace_id` (or that specific version) | expected, not a defect: never-persisted, TTL-expired, or a batched sink that has not flushed yet — an immediately-after-calculate `Explain` can legitimately miss |
+| `limen.ErrUnsupportedTraceVersion` | the record's `schema_version` is not the supported generation: pre-v2 (never served, never up-converted) or newer than this SDK | pre-v2: re-run the calculation — traces are re-derivable from inputs by the deterministic engine. Newer: upgrade the SDK doing the reading |
+| `*limen.ValidationError` | malformed read request (empty trace ID, version < 1) | fix the call |
+

+custom `TraceReader` is covered by the same guard automatically — it must
+not (and need not) implement its own version filtering, and must never
+up-convert (§7).
+
+`limen.ErrAuditDropped` belongs to the write side: a sink wraps it to report
+an intentional discard (sampling, back-pressure policy), which surfaces as
+`AuditStatus: "dropped"` rather than `"failed"`. A calculation never fails
+because its trace could not be persisted.

+## 6. Worked example: recomputing a trace ID by hand
+
+The contract's teeth: any stored envelope substantiates its own identity.
+This is a real envelope, emitted by the SDK for the covered-call snapshot in
+[consuming.md's quick start](../consuming.md#quick-start-rules-only-baseline-no-database-no-audit)

+rulebook `rules/cboe_baseline.yaml` at the revision this document was
+written against):
+
+```json

+  "schema_version": 2,
+  "version": 1,
+  "trace_id": "910d6b1e83afcb301cb5081e0fb37d7a",
+  "account_id": "ACC-1",
+  "position_id": "ACC-1",
+  "account_type": "margin",
+  "phase": "initial",
+  "currency": "USD",
+  "regime": { "family": "reg_t_strategy" },
+  "positions_sha": "3b5ac3ba35289b75edf680e6804b2e0afe6feb002de40764af74c5c46f54c4c3",
+  "bookkeeping_sha": "86df25118e342308ff260998334e70cf5e38c30f2092678449fe1f4bd76e1fd1",
+  "as_of": "2026-09-01T12:00:00Z",
+  "txn_cutoff": "2026-09-01T12:00:00Z",
+  "complete": true,
+  "outcome": "matched",

+```sh

+  'ACC-1' \
+  '3b5ac3ba35289b75edf680e6804b2e0afe6feb002de40764af74c5c46f54c4c3' \
+  'bcfac1583e11b30d18aa723a17bc5e143e5240971414d7e4fb28583b83e871a3' \
+  '' '' '' \
+  '2026-09-01T12:00:00Z' \
+  '2026-09-01T12:00:00Z' \
+  'decompose=false' \
+  'account_type=margin' \
+  'phase=initial' \
+  'currency=USD' \
+  'bookkeeping=86df25118e342308ff260998334e70cf5e38c30f2092678449fe1f4bd76e1fd1' \

+```

+## 7. Custom sink and reader obligations
+
+Hosts using `pkg/limenmongo` inherit all of this from the reference adapter

+implementing its own `limen.AuditSink` / `limen.TraceReader` — over

+storage-agnostically:
+

+

+   `schema_version` and `version` exactly as emitted (the SDK stamps
+   `schema_version: 2`, `version: 1`). Never strip, rename, or mutate
+   fields — the record must stay self-substantiating (§6).
body:

+limen internals.

+`schema_version: 2` is refused with a typed error (§5). Pre-v2 records are
+development debris carrying known-incomplete identities — never audit
+history.
+
+Two version fields appear throughout; they are distinct:

+| Field | Meaning | Changes when |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `schema_version` | envelope **shape** generation (currently `2`) | limen changes the persisted document shape (a compat event) |
+| `version` | **supersede counter** for one `trace_id` (starts at `1`) | a different payload is written under an existing `trace_id` (§4) |

+## 1. Guarantees and obligations at a glance
+
+What limen guarantees:
+
+- **Identity completeness.** Two calculations share a `trace_id` only when
+  every result-changing input is identical (§3). Cash-vs-margin,
+  initial-vs-maintenance, or bookkeeping-differing calculations over the
+  same positions get distinct IDs.
+- **Determinism and re-derivability.** The engine is deterministic and
+  clock-free: identical inputs produce identical numbers, so any trace is
+  re-derivable by re-running the calculation. This is also the remedy for an
+  unsupported-version record.
+- **Self-substantiation.** A persisted envelope carries every field its own
+  `trace_id` was derived from, so the ID can be recomputed and verified from
+  the stored record alone — no re-run required (§6). The ID is a seal, not
+  an assertion: a content hash proves, a UUID would only claim.
+- **Pre-computability.** The ID is derivable from the request alone; a host
+  can compute it before calculating.
+- **Supersede, never destroy.** A corrected number never erases the receipt
+  for the old one; `Explain` serves the latest and discloses priors (§4).
+- **Typed errors.** Every read-side failure mode is a sentinel or typed
+  error matched with `errors.Is`/`errors.As` (§5). Messages are not
+  contract.
+
+What the host owns:
+
+- **Storage and durability.** Audit emission is best-effort by contract: a
+  sink error degrades `CalculationResult.AuditStatus`, never fails the
+  calculation. Durability is the sink's job, and the sink is host-supplied
+  (the reference Mongo adapter or a custom one, §7).
+- **Retention.** Trace TTL/archival is host policy
+  ([sdk-result-integrity D5](../architecture/decisions/sdk-result-integrity.md#d5--ttldays-is-deleted-from-runtime-options-retention-is-host-policy-enacted-only-through-migration)),
+  enacted through the host's own migration tooling — for the Mongo adapter,
+  `cmd/migrate` per [operations.md](../operations.md#required-indexes-host-contract).

+  the versioning and never-destroy obligations of §7 — they are properties
+  of the store, not of limen's code.
+- **Churn monitoring.** Superseding writes are legitimate only around a
+  software upgrade; the host watches the churn signal (§4).

+Every emission is one envelope (Go: `limen.AuditEnvelope` on the write side,
+`limen.TraceRecord` on the read side — same fields, same JSON names). Two
+envelope kinds exist, distinguished by role, not shape:
+
+- **Account envelope** — one per calculation. `position_id` carries the
+  account ID (deliberately, so one field keys both envelope kinds);
+  `positions_sha` seals the full position set.
+- **Decomposition envelope** — one per position on the `Decompose: true`
+  path, in addition to the account envelope. `position_id` is the position
+  ID; `positions_sha` is that single position's content seal.

+Fields hosts may rely on, by JSON name:

+| Field | Type | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `schema_version` | int | always `2`; route/refuse on it before parsing anything else |
+| `version` | int | supersede counter, ≥ 1 (§4) |
+| `trace_id` | string | 32 hex chars, content-derived (§3) |
+| `account_id` | string | owning account |
+| `position_id` | string | account ID on account envelopes; position ID on decomposition envelopes |
+| `account_type` | string | `margin` \| `cash` — participates in the ID |

Not part of the ID — the rulebook seal already pins methodology |
+| `positions_sha` | string | SHA-256 (RFC 8785 canonical JSON) of the position content the evaluation saw |
+| `bookkeeping_sha` | string | seal of the bookkeeping scalars; always present — a zero-value bookkeeping seals as its own hash |
+| `policy_sha` | string | seal of host policy facts; **empty exactly when policy was absent from the ID recipe** (§3) |
+| `overlay_rulebook_hash` | string | house overlay rulebook seal; empty on baseline-only calculations |
+| `refdata_sha` | string | reference-data seal; empty on baseline-only calculations (refdata is never read there) |
+| `overrides_sha` | string | seal of the applied override set |
+| `as_of`, `txn_cutoff` | timestamp | bitemporal coordinates, stored truncated to millisecond precision (§3) |
+| `decompose` | bool | which aggregation pipeline ran |
+| `applied_overrides` | array | the exact sorted set `overrides_sha` seals, echoed for auditability |
+| `complete` | bool | true exactly when every position contributed to totals; gate on it before trusting any total in the trace body |

+| `outcome` | string | derived classification: `matched` \| `not_permitted` \| `incomplete` \| `error` at account level; the trace body's own outcome (e.g. `decomposed`) on decomposition envelopes |

+encoding); a verifier must treat a missing `refdata_sha` as `""`.

+All seals are SHA-256 hex over RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of the mapped
+calculation inputs. A host can precompute them for its own snapshot with
+`CalculationSnapshot.Hashes()` and match them against the envelope —
+`positions_sha` and `bookkeeping_sha` are byte-identical to
+`SnapshotHashes.Positions` / `.Bookkeeping` over the same values.

+## 3. Identity: what makes two calculations "the same"
+
+([trace-schema-v2 D1](../architecture/decisions/trace-schema-v2.md#d1--trace-identity-is-completed-content-addressing-the-sink-supersedes-with-lineage-never-silently-replaces))

+else is.** Same ID ⇒ same calculation (same question, same inputs); a
+retried emit of the same evaluation reuses the ID (idempotency is the
+feature). Distinct calculations can never legitimately share an ID.

+2. `positions_sha`
+3. `trace.rulebook_sha`
+4. `overlay_rulebook_hash` (empty string on baseline-only)
+5. `refdata_sha` (empty string on baseline-only)
+6. `overrides_sha` (empty string when none applied)

When the sole leg is short stock and `short_sale_proceeds` is omitted, zero, or negative, this exemption suppresses `CodeDecomposeStockResidual`, but the baseline `short_stock` rule requires that field to be positive. The optimizer converts that requires failure into a residual no-rule outcome, so `Decompose: true` produces an incomplete calculation even though preflight no longer reports the gap. Restrict the exemption to long stock or to short stock with positive proceeds.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject mixed stock symbols until each has its own price**

When a position contains `StockKind` legs for differently priced symbols—the newly supported mixed-stock case—this scopes the legs but leaves the position's single `U` unchanged. `derivePositionFacts` therefore prices every symbol through the same `U`, so a percentage override targeting a later symbol can silently use another symbol's price and materially misstate the house requirement. Because stock legs have no per-leg current-price field, either reject multiple stock symbols in one position or add/normalize a price per symbol before deriving these bases.
